SECURITY (dropped.rs + lib.rs)
- Allow-list: read_capped refuses unless allowed.iter().any(|p| p == path). Path equality compares components, so it only folds repeated separators and "." components (same file); ".." is not normalised and no canonicalize() is called, so it cannot widen the set. The list comes only from WindowEvent::DragDrop(Drop{paths}) in on_window_event and is replaced on every drop.
- Order of checks: allow-list, then the extension (7, case-insensitive), then symlink_metadata().file_type().is_file() before any open (refuses symlinks, folders, FIFOs and devices without blocking on a FIFO), then the opened handle's metadata().is_file(), then len > 20 MiB, then take(MAX+1).read_to_end and refuse if more than MAX came back. All of these match the plan.
- read_dropped_file is in both generate_handler! lists. There is exactly one on_window_event, shared by both builds. The #[cfg(feature="native-smoke")] CloseRequested -> smoke::record_window_close() is kept inside it, as in HEAD. A poisoned mutex is skipped, not a panic. The async command clones the list under the lock and then reads, so no lock is held during I/O.
- Capabilities: T080 adds none. The default.json diff (core:window:allow-set-theme) belongs to T075. core:default includes core:event:default = allow-listen/allow-unlisten/allow-emit/allow-emit-to (acl-manifests.json), so onDragDropEvent is permitted. App commands have no app manifest (build.rs is plain tauri_build::build()), so read_dropped_file needs no permission entry.
- Non-blocking notes: (a) one-shot consumption would be a better design. Removing the path after a successful read costs 2-3 lines and no UX, because the UI reads once per drop, and it would stop the page re-reading a dropped file (for example after the user edits it) without a new drop. I recommend it as a follow-up. Replace-per-drop is acceptable. (b) There is a TOCTOU gap between symlink_metadata and File::open: a symlink swapped in would be followed, and the post-open is_file sees the target. Exploiting it needs write access to a path the user just dropped. Accepted. O_NOFOLLOW via OpenOptionsExt::custom_flags would close it. (c) Only parent-directory symlinks inside a user-dropped path are followed, which is the user's choice. (d) Event routing: the plan's fallback was to record paths in both on_window_event and on_webview_event. The owner recorded only WindowEvent, based on the source reading in the plan's Context. Acceptable, but if the owner's Finder drag shows nothing, adding an on_webview_event recorder is the ~6-line fix.

FRONTEND
- dropImport.ts: dropProblem returns "Drop one file at a time." for anything other than exactly one file, null for the 7 extensions (case-insensitive), and otherwise the import-type message. readDroppedPath invokes read_dropped_file and wraps the bytes in new File([bytes], baseName(path)). The type is empty, which is fine because previewWriting routes by extension. listenForNativeDrops uses getCurrentWebview().onDragDropEvent: enter with paths -> hover on; leave -> off; drop -> off, then onDrop. It returns the unlisten function, which ProjectLibrary calls on unmount with a disposed guard.
- ProjectLibrary.tsx: dragenter, dragleave and drop are gated on dataTransfer.types.includes("Files"), and dragover preventDefaults only for files. A depth counter is reset on drop. data-dropping is set on <main>. dropEnabled gates the drop and the highlight; I accept the highlight gating as a reasonable extra. Errors go to onDropError. Native drops re-check dropEnabled and dropProblem on basenames.
- The document-level dragover/drop block runs only in the browser build (the desktop branch returns before installing it) and is NOT file-gated, contrary to the brief's wording. It does not touch the sidebar reorder, because App.tsx renders {!project ? <ProjectLibrary/> : <><ProjectSidebar .../>...}, so the two are never mounted together, and the effect cleanup removes both listeners on unmount. The only other draggable or onDrop handlers in src are in ProjectSidebar.tsx.
- library.css: .library[data-dropping] has outline 2px dashed var(--accent), outline-offset calc(-1 * var(--space-2)), and background color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 6%, var(--paper)). No pseudo-element text; the rest of the screen is radius 0.
- App.tsx: the two props are exactly as the plan specifies (dropEnabled={!busy && !importBusy && !importPreview && !nameDialog && !choice}, onDropError={(message) => setError(message)}). importWriting has no diff lines.
- Tests: 7 new projects-screen drop cases match plan step 7 and add a flicker case and a document-block case.

GIT STATUS: every modified or untracked path is T080's own or belongs to done tasks: T071 (Cargo.toml, smoke.rs, native-screens.*), T072/T073 (CSS files, designTokens, sidebar-selection spec), T074 (AGENTS.md, design-system.md), T075 (appearance.*, Segmented, main.tsx, capabilities), T076 (ProjectDialogs, ProjectSidebar, palette.test), T077 (ResearchPanel, research spec), T084 (notice spec), T085, and the plan folder plus team/*. scripts/__pycache__ was already there. Nothing is unexplained.

ONLY THE OWNER CAN PROVE (plan Validation 9c/9d): a real Finder drag onto the Mac app; whether onDragDropEvent registers in WKWebView and the dashed highlight appears in WebKit; whether DragDrop(Drop) reaches on_window_event and records the paths (WindowEvent vs WebviewEvent routing); whether read_dropped_file returns the bytes at runtime and the import preview opens (Cancel creates nothing); the .pdf and two-file error banners in the app; and whether the native sidebar section drag-reorder behaves as before (wry intercepts drags; this was unverified before this work too).
